console.warning: This is a browser tool for developers. If someone told you to paste something here to turn on a feature, fix a problem or get access, it is a scam. Code pasted here runs with this panel's access: it can change or switch off the firewall, as root, on every server the panel manages, and hand them to someone else.
console.advice: Do not paste anything here that you do not understand, and never share the address with #token= in it.
theme.label: Theme
language.label: Language
hosts.title: Hosts
host.removeConfirm: Remove {{name}} from the list? Nothing changes on the host itself.
host.sandboxNote: A private network namespace with a demo firewall. Nothing done here touches a real firewall.
platform.readOnly.title: OpenWrt: the firewall is shown, not changed
platform.readOnly.openwrt: OpenWrt keeps its firewall in UCI (/etc/config/firewall), which LuCI shows and fw4 turns into nftables. A table changed with nft directly would be gone after the next firewall reload and would never show in LuCI, so for now hopdeck only shows the firewall here. Changes through UCI come in a later version. Tracing packets works.
hostKey.title: Check the server's key
hostKey.titleChanged: Compare the old and the new key
hostKey.intro: hopdeck connects without logging in, reads the key the server presents and shows its fingerprint. Nothing is saved yet.
hostKey.verify: Compare the fingerprint with the one the server itself shows, on its console or through its administrator. On the server, this command prints it:
hostKey.confirmReplace: The host's administrator has confirmed that the new fingerprint is correct.
hostKey.backup: The old entry will be removed from {{file}}; ssh-keygen keeps the previous file with the .old extension.
override.label: Manual override
override.banner: hopdeck may change every table on this host, including those of other tools, until you switch it off or hopdeck stops.
override.warn: hopdeck will let you change tables it does not manage, including those of other tools such as Docker or firewalld, which may overwrite such changes or break because of them.
override.warnSafety: Validation, the diff and the automatic rollback still protect every change. It lasts until you switch it off or hopdeck stops.
tabs.label: Host sections
facts.title: System
access.sudoPasswordStored: Full access through sudo, with the password kept for this session
access.passwordHint: hopdeck keeps it in memory only while it runs and never saves it to disk.
access.noneTitle: nft cannot run as root on this host
access.noneHint: Log in as root, or allow this user to run nft with sudo.
access.nftMissing: nftables (the nft program) is not installed on this host
access.notAllowedTitle: sudo does not allow {{user}} to run nft
access.notAllowedHintGroup: As root, add {{user}} to the {{group}} group (usermod -aG {{group}} {{user}}), or allow nft for it in /etc/sudoers.d/. Group changes take effect after a new login.
access.notAllowedHint: As root, allow {{user}} to run nft with sudo, for example through the administrators group or a file in /etc/sudoers.d/. Group changes take effect after a new login.
access.restartNote: hopdeck keeps the groups of the session it was started from, so after the change start it again from a new login.
access.sudoMissingTitle: sudo is not installed on this host
access.sudoMissingHint: Log in as root, or install sudo and allow this user to run nft.
ruleset.empty.title: The ruleset is empty
ruleset.empty: nftables filters nothing on this host right now.
ruleset.unknown: Items hopdeck does not recognise: {{count}}. They are shown below exactly as nft printed them.
ruleset.truncated: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} lines. The Text tab has all of them.
live.label: Live
live.hint: How often hopdeck reads the counters and checks whether the rules changed on the host.
live.changed: The rules on the host changed since they were read
live.changedTables: Changed, added or removed: {{tables}}. What you see here is the earlier state.
live.rateTitle: Traffic through this rule since the previous read
editor.changedOnHost: This table changed on the host after the editor read it
editor.changedOnHostHint: Your version replaces the whole table, so it would undo that change. The review shows exactly what changes; refresh the rules and edit again to keep both.
persist.title: After a reboot
persist.unavailable: hopdeck cannot save changes for boot on this host
persist.noConfig: hopdeck found no file that loads nftables at boot.
persist.noInclude.title: The tables hopdeck manages are not loaded at boot
persist.noInclude: hopdeck saves them in {{directory}}, but {{file}} does not load that directory. With your consent, hopdeck adds this line at the end of the file:
persist.noInclude.safety: A dated copy of the file is kept, and nft checks the whole file afterwards; if nft rejects it, the copy is put back.
persist.guess: hopdeck found this file at its usual location; the nftables service did not name it.
persist.serviceOff.title: nftables.service is disabled
persist.serviceOff: Nothing loads the firewall at boot, including {{file}}.
persist.alsoInMain: Also defined in {{file}}: at boot hopdeck's copy replaces that definition, and deleting the table in hopdeck does not remove it from there.
table.adoptHint: hopdeck marks the table as its own and may change it from now on. Nothing else in the table changes.
newTable.title: New table
newTable.familyHint.inet: IPv4 and IPv6 together; the usual choice for a firewall.
newTable.familyHint.netdev: Traffic of one interface, before anything else sees it (ingress) or last of all (egress).
newTable.name: Name
newTable.templateHostHint: An input chain with policy drop. It lets in replies to this host's own connections, loopback, ping and IPv6 neighbour discovery, and blocks other incoming traffic. Forwarded and outgoing traffic are not affected. You can change all of it in the editor.
newTable.templateEmptyHint: A table without chains; you add them in the editor.
newTable.sshWarning: hopdeck reaches this host over SSH. Without this rule the new table would cut the connection off, and the safety check would roll the change back.
newTable.nothingYet: Nothing changes on the host yet: the table opens in the editor, and you review the change before it is applied.
newTable.problem.name: The name must start with a letter or _ and may contain only letters, digits, _ and -.
newTable.problem.taken: The host already has a table with this family and name.
deploy.title: Review the change
deploy.preparing: Checking the change on the host…
deploy.commandsRollback: Rollback, if you do not keep the change: the set gets back exactly the elements it has now.
deploy.valid: nft on the host accepts the change (nft -c).
deploy.invalid: nft rejects the change, so nothing will be applied
deploy.safety.title: How this change is protected
deploy.safety.systemd: A systemd unit on the host restores the previous state after {{seconds}} s unless you keep the change.
deploy.safety.detached: A background process on the host restores the previous state after {{seconds}} s unless you keep the change.
deploy.safety.unavailable: Nothing on this host could restore the previous state on its own, so hopdeck will not apply this.
deploy.safety.fresh: Right after applying, hopdeck opens a new SSH connection; if that fails, it undoes the change at once.
deploy.safety.atomic: The change is applied in one transaction: all of it or nothing. Only the tables above are touched.
deploy.overrideNote: This change relies on Manual override.
deploy.awaiting: Applied. Check that everything works, then keep the change.
deploy.countdown_one: Without a decision, the host rolls back in {{count}} second.
deploy.countdown_other: Without a decision, the host rolls back in {{count}} seconds.
deploy.freshFailedPending: New SSH connections failed and hopdeck could not undo the change through the existing one; the host will roll back at the deadline.
deploy.rolledBack.timeout: The host rolled the change back because it was not kept in time.
deploy.rolledBack.fresh: New SSH connections failed after the change, so hopdeck undid it at once.
deploy.failed: nft could not apply the change; nothing changed.
deploy.persisted.title: Saved for the next boot
deploy.persisted.notManaged: Not saved for boot, because hopdeck does not manage them: {{tables}}. What loads at boot is up to their owner.
deploy.persisted.problem: The change is live, but not saved for the next boot
path.traffic.label: Traffic
path.kind.label: Direction
path.howTo.title: How to read it
path.howTo: The packet passes the hooks from top to bottom. In each hook, the base chains of all tables run from the lowest priority up. accept ends only the current chain: later chains in the same hook, and later hooks, still see the packet. drop stops it at once, and so does a chain's drop policy. Click a chain to see its rules.
path.decision.routing: Routing decision: this host or onward
path.decision.bridge: Bridge decision: this host or onward
path.empty: No chains: nftables does not filter here.
path.tie: Same priority as another chain in this hook: their order is not guaranteed.
path.natNote: nat chains see only the first packet of each connection
chain.regular: regular chain, entered with jump or goto
chain.noRulesBase: No rules: the chain policy decides every packet.
chain.noRulesRegular: No rules: packets return to the chain that jumped here.
chain.name: Name
chain.kindBaseHint: Hooks into the packet path: packets reach it on their own, and its policy decides whatever the rules leave undecided.
chain.kindRegularHint: Packets get here only through jump or goto from another chain. Handy for grouping rules.
chain.problem.name: The name must start with a letter or _ and may contain only letters, digits, _ and -.
chain.problem.taken: The table already has a chain with this name.
chain.problem.device: Enter the interface the chain attaches to.
rule.handle: Rule handle: nft uses it to address this exact rule
rule.noText: nft printed no text for this rule, probably because the ruleset changed while hopdeck read it. Refresh to read it again. The rule as JSON:
editor.title: Editing {{table}}
editor.visualBlocked: The text was changed by hand and cannot be shown as a grid. Review it, or discard the changes to go back.
editor.rejected: The edited table was rejected, nothing was applied
editor.rejectedRows: Rules nft pointed at are marked in red.
editor.rejectedLines: Lines nft pointed at are marked in red.
editor.textNote: The whole table in nft syntax. nft on the host checks it before anything is applied, and you review the difference first.
editor.notFound: Table {{table}} is not in nft's listing. Refresh the ruleset and try again.
editor.gone: Table {{table}} no longer exists on the host
editor.textRuleTitle: The form cannot show this rule without losing part of it, so it is edited as nft text.
editor.noChains: The table has no chains yet. A base chain hooks into the packet path; a regular chain is reached with jump or goto.
trace.intro: hopdeck marks the packets that match the filter and shows the way each one takes through your chains and rules, and which rule or policy decided. A temporary table does the marking; it changes nothing about what happens to packets and is removed at the end, by the host itself if the panel is gone.
trace.rateHint: At most this many packets a second are traced, so busy traffic cannot flood the panel.
trace.cleanupFailed: Removing {{table}} did not go as expected
trace.tableHint: The host removes it by itself at {{time}} at the latest.
trace.waitingHint: Send the traffic you want to see now, e.g. connect from the other machine.
trace.noChains: No chain of the firewall sees packets here, so it went through: nothing stops a packet by default.
trace.passed: Passed through without a matching rule.
error.invalid-filter.title: The trace filter is not valid
error.invalid-filter.hint: Fields take values only: addresses, prefixes, ports, ranges or lists separated by commas.
error.trace-unavailable.title: Tracing is not possible here
error.trace-unavailable.hint: hopdeck traces only when the host itself can remove the tracing table later. Log in as root, or allow systemd-run through sudo.
error.trace-not-found.title: This trace no longer exists
error.trace-not-found.hint: hopdeck keeps traces in memory only; they are gone after a restart.
error.platform-read-only.title: hopdeck does not change the firewall on this host yet
trace.running_one: Tracing: {{count}} packet so far, {{seconds}} s left
trace.running_other: Tracing: {{count}} packets so far, {{seconds}} s left
trace.finished_one: Tracing finished with {{count}} packet; the tracing table is removed.
trace.finished_other: Tracing finished with {{count}} packets; the tracing table is removed.
set.elementsNote: One element per line. Saving recreates the set with these elements as they were when the editor opened; to change only elements, use the Elements button in the rules view.
set.kindSetHint: A list of values that rules refer to as @name, e.g. ip saddr @blocked drop.
set.kindMapHint: Pairs of a key and a value that rules look up, e.g. tcp dport vmap @ports picks a verdict for each port.
set.intervalHint: Prefixes (10.0.0.0/24) and ranges (1000-2000) need the option "prefixes and ranges".
set.problem.taken: The table already has a set or map with this name.
editor.setsNote: Elements of existing sets change in place with the Elements button in the rules view, without replacing the table.
elements.more: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} matching elements; narrow the search to see the rest.
elements.problem.quote: A comment cannot contain a double quote.
elements.problem.value: Choose the value for the map.
elements.problem.exists: This element is already there; to replace it, remove it first.
rule.flagsAny: one of the set flags is enough
rule.flagsHint: Click a flag to require it set, again to require it clear, once more to ignore it.
rule.rpfilterOn: source address not routable back through the incoming interface
rule.rpfilterHint: Matches packets with a spoofed source address, like rp_filter; usually with drop in a prerouting chain.
rule.limitHint: Within the limit, the rule matches packets up to the rate (e.g. accept 10/second). Over the limit, it matches only the excess (e.g. drop).
rule.keyedLimitHint: Each address gets its own limit, e.g. at most 3 new SSH connections a minute from one address. nft creates the set if it does not exist yet.
rule.connLimitHint: Concurrent connections tracked by conntrack that match this rule.
rule.quotaHint: Counts bytes until the quota is used up; "over the limit" matches the traffic after that.
rule.vmapHint: A named map (@name) or elements such as 22 : accept, 80 : drop.
rule.logGroupHint: Sends packets to userspace through nflog instead of the kernel log, e.g. to ulogd.
rule.notrackOn: do not track the connection (raw chains)
rule.problem.tcpProtocol: TCP flags need the protocol tcp.
rule.problem.vmap: Choose what to look up by and the map.
rule.problem.keyedLimit: The per-source limit needs a rate, a key and a set name (letters, digits, _ and -).
rule.problem.connLimit: The connection count must be a whole number.
rule.problem.quota: The quota must be a positive number.
rule.problem.logGroup: The nflog group must be a number from 0 to 65535.
rule.valuesHint: Separate several values with commas (80, 443), write a range with a dash (1000-2000), refer to a named set as @name.
rule.textOnly: The form cannot show this rule without losing part of it, so it is edited as nft text.
rule.byIndexTitle: Match the interface index (iif/oif): faster, but only for interfaces that exist when the rule is loaded.
rule.problem.portProtocol: Ports need the protocol tcp, udp, udplite, sctp or dccp.
rule.problem.icmpProtocol: An ICMP type needs the protocol icmp or icmpv6.
rule.problem.target: Choose the chain to jump to.
rule.problem.natTo: Enter the address to translate to.
rule.problem.redirect: Enter the port to redirect to.
rule.problem.limit: The rate limit must be a positive number.
rule.problem.quote: Log prefixes and comments cannot contain a double quote.
rule.problem.text: Enter the rule as one line of nft text.
owner.tool: Probably created by {{tool}}: recognised by the table name. hopdeck will not change it.
owner.evidence.marker: nft reports that iptables-nft manages this table.
owner.evidence.xt: Its rules contain xt expressions, which only iptables-nft can recreate.
owner.evidence.chains: Its chain names are the ones iptables uses, such as INPUT and FORWARD.
owner.iptables: Change it with iptables, not nft: hopdeck treats it as read-only.

error.ssh-host-key-changed.hint: Someone may be intercepting the connection. Do not continue until the host's administrator confirms the new key.

error.spawn-failed.hint: The message below names the program hopdeck could not start.
error.command-failed.title: The command failed on the host
error.nft-missing.title: nftables (the nft program) is not installed on this host
error.no-privileges.title: nft cannot run as root on this host
error.password-required.title: Enter the sudo password first

error.internal-error.hint: The terminal where hopdeck runs shows more. Please report this error.

error.invalid-ruleset.title: hopdeck cannot read what nft printed

error.host-key-mismatch.title: The server's key changed while you were checking it

error.deployment-state.title: This change is no longer at that step

error.deployment-not-found.title: This change no longer exists

addHost.title: Add SSH host
addHost.destinationHint: For example admin@fw1.example.com, or a Host alias from ~/.ssh/config. hopdeck uses your SSH configuration, keys and agent.
addHost.name: Display name (optional)
deploy.restoring: Puts back version #{{version}} from the history.
deploy.recorded: Recorded in the host's history as version #{{version}}.
deploy.notRecorded: The change is kept, but it is missing from the host's history
history.failure: Recording a version failed at {{time}}, so a change may be missing
history.unreadable: The description of these versions cannot be read: {{versions}}.
history.empty: No history yet. hopdeck records a version each time a change to a table it manages is kept, and when it notices that one changed outside hopdeck.
history.restoreNothing: The managed tables are already like this version.
history.noEarlier: No earlier version is kept, so every table shows as added.
history.noConnection: no SSH: this computer or the sandbox
history.override: on: tables hopdeck does not manage could be changed
history.authorNote: The user and computer are what the hopdeck that made the change reported about itself. The login, address and key are what the host saw: the SSH connection and sshd's log line for it.
history.noticedNote: Something other than hopdeck changed the managed tables; who is not known. Shown here is when a hopdeck noticed, and whose. Several changes between two looks show as one.
history.baselineNote: The managed tables as hopdeck first found them on this host.
history.noTables: No managed tables on either side.
settings.historyUsage_one: It takes {{size}} for {{count}} version. Beyond the limit the oldest versions go; the last {{min}} always stay.
settings.historyUsage_other: It takes {{size}} for {{count}} versions. Beyond the limit the oldest versions go; the last {{min}} always stay.
settings.sharedNote: Kept on the host in {{file}}, so everyone who manages this host shares these settings.
error.version-not-found.title: There is no such version in the history
error.version-not-found.hint: It may have been removed to keep the history within its size limit.
table.resizeHint: Drag to change the width, or use the arrow keys. Double-click to fit the content again.
deploy.inPlace: Rule by rule: {{changes}}. The other rules keep their handles, counters and limits; a rollback puts back the whole table.
deploy.inPlace.nothing: No rule changes; the table stays as it is.
deploy.wholeTable: The whole table is replaced in one transaction, because more than its rules changes (a chain, its policy, a set or the table itself). Rules copied unchanged keep their counter values as read; changed rules count from zero.

usage.label: Load on the host
usage.cpuHint_one: {{count}} thread: 100% is one fully busy thread, {{max}}% all of them.
usage.cpuHint_other: {{count}} threads: 100% is one fully busy thread, {{max}}% all of them.
usage.ramHint: Memory in use, as free counts it: the total less what is available.
sshKeys.title: SSH keys for this host
sshKeys.intro: ssh offers these keys to the host. A key with a passphrase needs it once: the agent then keeps the key unlocked for as long as you choose. hopdeck keeps the passphrase nowhere.
sshKeys.allOpen: ssh offers these keys to the host, and none is locked (each has no passphrase, or is unlocked in the agent), yet the host accepts none of them. Put one on the host below, or check the user in your SSH configuration.
sshKeys.none: Your SSH configuration names no key for this host that exists on this computer (ssh -G shows which files ssh tries).
sshKeys.lifetime.session: until you log out of this computer
sshKeys.agent.session: Unlocked keys go to the ssh-agent of your login session, so ssh in your terminal can use them too.
sshKeys.agent.hopdeck: Your session runs no ssh-agent, so hopdeck runs its own; the keys it holds are gone when hopdeck stops.
sshKeys.agent.windows: Unlocked keys go to Windows' OpenSSH agent service, which ssh in your terminal uses too. That agent takes no time limit, so hopdeck removes the key when its time is up, or when hopdeck stops; without a limit, Windows keeps it, also across restarts, until you remove it (ssh-add -D).
sshKeys.agent.none: No ssh-agent runs in your session, and hopdeck could not start its own, so a key with a passphrase cannot be unlocked here. Install the OpenSSH client's ssh-agent, or unlock the key in a terminal (ssh-add) before starting hopdeck.
error.wrong-passphrase.title: That passphrase does not open the key
error.wrong-passphrase.hint: Nothing was added to the agent. Try again.
keySetup.title: Is the key not on the host yet?
keySetup.intro: hopdeck can log in once with the account's password, add the key to the account's authorized_keys as ssh-copy-id does, and check with a new connection that the key alone gets in. The password serves that login only and is kept nowhere; logging in with it keeps working.
keySetup.password: The account's password on the host
keySetup.run: Put the key on the host
keySetup.lockedNote: This key needs its passphrase: hopdeck puts it on the host, and tries it once you unlock it above.
keySetup.works: The key is in {{file}} on the host, and it logs in on its own
keySetup.unverified: The key is in {{file}} on the host
keySetup.unverifiedHint: It needs its passphrase, so hopdeck could not try it yet: unlock it above, and hopdeck connects with it.
keySetup.refused: The key is in {{file}}, but the host does not take it
keySetup.blocker.pubkeyauthentication: sshd has logging in with keys off (PubkeyAuthentication {{value}}).
keySetup.blocker.authenticationmethods: sshd wants more than a key to log in (AuthenticationMethods {{value}}).
keySetup.blocker.permitrootlogin: sshd does not let root log in (PermitRootLogin {{value}}). hopdeck leaves that to you: log in as another account that has sudo, or change it yourself.
keySetup.blocker.authorizedkeysfile: sshd reads keys from {{value}}, not from ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, where hopdeck put the key.
keySetup.blocker.pubkeyacceptedalgorithm: sshd takes no {{value}} keys (PubkeyAcceptedAlgorithms). Use another key, such as ed25519.
keySetup.blocker.home: Others may write to the home directory ({{value}}), and sshd then ignores its keys (StrictModes). On the host: chmod go-w ~
keySetup.noBlockers: sshd's configuration lets this key in for this login. sshd's log on the host says why it did not (journalctl -u ssh, or /var/log/auth.log).
keySetup.unread: hopdeck could not read sshd's configuration for this login: that takes root, or sudo.
keySetup.checkYourself: To look yourself, as root on the host:
keySetup.dropbear: The host runs dropbear, which takes keys from authorized_keys with nothing to switch on. Check the permissions of {{file}} and the directories above it.
keySetup.unknownServer: hopdeck found neither sshd nor dropbear on the host, so it cannot say more.
keySetup.allowIntro: These lines let keys in; hopdeck can write them to {{file}} and reload sshd:
keySetup.allowKeeps: They only add a way in: logging in with a password works as before. hopdeck checks the file with sshd -t first, and puts everything back if sshd would not use it.
keySetup.allowed.applied: hopdeck wrote these lines to {{file}} and reloaded sshd:
keySetup.allowed.overridden: sshd would not use the lines: something else in its configuration wins, usually a Match block or a file read before {{file}}. hopdeck removed them again. What sshd uses:
keySetup.allowed.no-directory: sshd has no sshd_config.d directory, so hopdeck wrote nothing. Add the lines near the top of /etc/ssh/sshd_config, before any Match block, and reload sshd.
keySetup.allowed.invalid: sshd -t rejected the file, so hopdeck removed it again:
keySetup.allowed.unreadable: sshd -T failed with the file in place, so hopdeck removed it again:
keySetup.allowed.reload-failed: sshd would not reload, so hopdeck removed the file again:
error.login-password-rejected.title: The host did not take the password
error.login-password-rejected.hint: The account's password on the host is asked for here, not the passphrase of the key; check it and the keyboard layout (the eye in the field shows what it holds), and that the browser did not fill the field with a saved password. The host may also refuse passwords for this account only: sshd lets root log in with a key alone by default (PermitRootLogin prohibit-password).
error.password-login-disabled.title: The host takes no passwords
error.password-login-disabled.hint: sshd accepts keys only (PasswordAuthentication no), so hopdeck cannot log in to put the key there. Add it to the account's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys another way, for example from your provider's console.
host.loginLost: The host stopped letting hopdeck in
host.loginLostHint: A new SSH connection was refused. A key unlocked for a limited time has probably left the agent: unlock it again below, and hopdeck reconnects.
keyGen.title: Generate a new key
keyGen.intro: hopdeck makes a new key pair in ~/.ssh with ssh-keygen. Ed25519 is short, fast and the safe choice; RSA is for servers that take nothing else.
keyGen.name: File name in ~/.ssh
keyGen.noPassphrase: Without a passphrase, anyone who gets the key's file can log in with it wherever it is put, with nothing to stop them. With one, the file alone is not enough, and the agent still spares you typing it each time.
keyGen.use.hopdeck: hopdeck offers it, and keeps that itself; ~/.ssh/config stays as it is
